title: Fourteen Springs and One Short Note
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·情感与情绪）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·情感与情绪）　|　核心词汇：doubt　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 doubt 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 my teacher ① raised a doubt that no colleague in the room would have answered, and he said the raising was the whole of the spring. The ② doubt, meaning the question and not the belief, ran fourteen springs and stayed unnamed in the book; a doubt, he said, is the only thing in a room that is judged by how long it is left unanswered.

Every ③ doubt in that room had the same short note at the end of it, and the ④ doubt at the end, meaning the one they kept for themselves and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A doubt, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to answer; my teacher said the answering is the part that fills fourteen springs.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the doubt was the whole of the story, meaning the uncertainty and not the question. The ⑥ doubt, meaning the uncertainty and not any of that, is the only thing in a story that everybody raises and nobody settles; doubt, he said, is either something you raise or the only word that means both a question and an uncertainty. He said the uncertainty is the part they remember.

By 1964 the ⑦ doubt had become a line in a letter, and the letter had become an argument about the short note. The ⑧ doubt of the whole thing, my teacher wrote in April, was one room and fourteen springs of answering; doubt, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to answer. She said the answering was never mentioned.

The ⑨ doubt I remember is the one named in the letter, which was settled in 1976 and is still described as the quietest in the room. A ⑩ doubt, my mother said in 1978, is the only one that improves by being answered; every doubt, she said, is an uncertainty that has agreed to look like a question. She said the uncertainty was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 怀疑；疑问（指那间屋子里提出来的那一个）
B. n. 怀疑；疑问（指那份疑虑本身，与信念相对）
C. 固定搭配：raise a doubt 提出一个疑问
D. n. 怀疑；疑问（指留给自己的那一份）
E. n. 怀疑；疑问（抽象总称，指一家人的疑虑之事）
F. n. 怀疑；疑问（指信里写到、被列名的那一个）
G. n. 不确定；悬而未决（指故事里人人提起却无人解决的那样东西）
H. n. 不确定（抽象总称，指人人提起却无人解决的那种状态）

items.q: raised a doubt that no colleague in the room would have answered
The doubt, meaning the question and not the belief
the doubt was the whole of the story
the doubt had become a line in a letter
The doubt of the whole thing
A doubt, my mother said in 1978

answers.why: raise a doubt 意为“提出一个疑问”，1955 年老师提出了一个屋子里没有一位同事肯回答的疑问。
doubt 意为“怀疑、疑问”，指那份疑虑本身而不是信念，它经过了十四个春天而在簿子上没有被记名。
doubt 意为“怀疑、疑问”，指那间屋子里的每一个疑问，每一个到头来都有同一张短短的字条。
doubt 意为“怀疑、疑问”，指留给自己的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
doubt 意为“不确定、悬而未决”，指故事里人人提起却无人解决的那样东西，叔叔说这份不确定就是那个故事的全部。
doubt 意为“不确定”，指人人提起却无人解决的那种状态而不是那份疑虑，是故事里人人都提、却无人解决的东西。
doubt 意为“怀疑、疑问”，指信里写到、被列名的那一个，到 1964 年这个疑问成了信里的一行。
doubt 意为“怀疑、疑问”，老师四月写道，整件事的疑虑之事是一间屋子和十四个春天的作答。
doubt 意为“怀疑、疑问”，我记得的是信里列名的那一个，1976 年被解决了，至今仍被说成屋子里最安静的一个。
doubt 为抽象总称，母亲 1978 年说，一份怀疑是唯一会因为被好好作答而变得更好的东西。
